newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage rates fell again this week - Freddie Mac.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage rates fell again this week - Freddie Mac.

text.p: Fixed-rate home mortgages fell this week to their lowest levels since December, while adjustable loans are the most affordable in almost a year, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp., or Freddie Mac, said Thursday.

Thirty-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 7.56 percent, the lowest since 7.44 percent in the week ended Dec. 6. Fifteen-year loans fell to 7.06 percent, the lowest since 7.06 percent in the week ended Dec. 13.
Last week, the 30-year rate averaged 7.65 percent, and the 15-year 7.14 percent.
Adjustable mortgages rates fell to 5.45 percent from 5.52 percent in last week. The rate is the lowest since 5.40 percent in the week ended March 8, 1996.
A year ago, the 30-year loan rate averaged 7.32 percent, the 15-year 6.77 percent and the adjustable loan 5.34 percent.
Freddie Mac said the most recent batch of economic statistics indicated no bad news about inflation.
Freddie Mac Deputy Chief Economist Frank Nothaft said reports showing lower wholesale prices and a slight gain in consumer prices during January will mean a further drop in interest rates this week.
"This good news on the inflation front translates into lower interest rates this week," Nothaft said. "It should also be a good backdrop for continuing strength in the housing market."

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average of 1.7 percent in fees and points on both 30- and 15-year loans, unchanged from last week. Charges on adjustable loans edged up to 1.4 percent from 1.3 percent last week.
